children.name: Intro
children.text: Sigma is a design tool for building a design system and designing with it, right in your browser. Your files are saved in this browser; nothing leaves it unless you download or export it.

children.name: Bullet
children.text: •  Sigma Design files have a canvas: pages, frames, components and layouts. This file is one.

children.name: Bullet
children.text: •  Sigma Tokens files hold design tokens (colors, spacing, type, shadows, motion) and have no canvas. They’re published for Sigma Design files to use.

children.name: Bullet
children.text: •  Sigma Icons files hold icons imported from SVG (from a free set like Lucide), for components to use. No canvas either.

children.name: This file uses the Sigma Tokens and Sigm
children.text: This file uses the Sigma Tokens and Sigma Icons files next to it in the Welcome to Sigma folder on the files home. Every color, size, text style and shadow here comes from one of its tokens, so switching a mode or a brand restyles everything at once.

children.name: When a Sigma Tokens or Sigma Icons file
children.text: When a Sigma Tokens or Sigma Icons file publishes a new version, the Sigma Design files that use it are offered the update.

children.name: Your files also have Optics, a design sy
children.text: Your files also have Optics, a design system made in Sigma and inspired by Shopify’s Polaris: Optics Tokens (in Sigma Tokens), Optics Icons (in Sigma Icons), and Optics Foundations and Optics Components (in Sigma Design), with color, type, spacing, elevation, motion, icons and documented, ready components. They’re yours to change. Link Optics Tokens and Optics Components from your own files to design with them; Sigma Tokens ▾ → Add Optics design system adds them again.

children.name: Bullet
children.text: •  Layers and Assets are on the left. The right panel shows what you’ve selected, or this file’s tokens and libraries when nothing is.

children.name: Bullet
children.text: •  The Σ menu has your files, export, version history, tokens, libraries and the keyboard shortcuts (press ?).

children.name: Bullet
children.text: •  Back to files (Σ menu) goes to the files home, where this file and its tokens are in the Welcome to Sigma folder. Deleted files wait in the Archive until you delete them forever.

This file is a playground: change anything, nothing is saved, and it’s back to the original the next time you open it. Duplicate to keep changes (in the banner) makes it your own.

children.name: Intro
children.text: Draw, select and arrange layers on an infinite canvas. Most of it works the way it does in Figma.

children.name: Bullet
children.text: •  Click selects; ⇧-click adds. Drag on the canvas for a marquee.

children.name: Bullet
children.text: •  ⌘-click selects deep inside groups and frames; double-click or Enter goes one level in, ⇧Enter one level out.

children.name: Bullet
children.text: •  Dragging snaps to other layers with red guides; hold ⌘ to place freely. Hold ⌥ to measure distances.

children.name: Bullet
children.text: •  ⌥-drag or ⌘D duplicates; arrow keys nudge by 1 (⇧ for 10).

children.name: Zoom; scroll or Space-drag to pan
children.text: Zoom; scroll or Space-drag to pan

children.name: Select two shapes on the right and press
children.text: Select two shapes on the right and press ⌘G to group them, then ⇧H to flip the group. Double-click the text to edit it. ⌘Z undoes anything.

children.name: Caption
children.text: Every color here comes from a primitive token.

children.name: Intro
children.text: Auto layout arranges layers in a row or a column, so designs adjust as content changes. Constraints and layout grids handle the rest.

children.name: Bullet
children.text: •  Set the direction, gap, padding and alignment in the Auto layout section. Gap and padding can use spacing tokens.

children.name: Bullet
children.text: •  Drag a layer inside to reorder it, or use the arrow keys. Absolute position takes a layer out of the flow.

children.name: Add auto layout to a frame or the selection
children.text: Add auto layout to a frame or the selection

children.name: Bullet
children.text: •  Each layer is Fixed, Hug (fits its contents) or Fill (takes the space left), set per direction.

children.name: Bullet
children.text: •  The link button next to W and H locks the aspect ratio.

children.name: Layers placed freely in a frame keep the
children.text: Layers placed freely in a frame keep their place when the frame is resized: Left, Right, Left & right, Center or Scale (and the same vertically). Hold ⌘ while resizing to ignore them.

children.name: Frames can have column, row and square g
children.text: Frames can have column, row and square grids, drawn on the canvas only. Layers snap to them, and ⌃G shows or hides them. Count, gutter and margin can use tokens, like the 12-column grid on the right.

children.name: Select a tag and press ⌘D: the row grows
children.text: Select a tag and press ⌘D: the row grows. Resize the Constraints frame by a corner and watch its layers keep their places.

children.name: Note
children.text: The row hugs its tags; each tag hugs its label.

children.name: A fixed-width column; its rows fill it.
children.text: A fixed-width column; its rows fill it.

children.name: Label
children.text: Padding and gap are space tokens

children.name: Body
children.text:
12 columns. The gutter and margin are layout tokens that point at the spacing scale.
Press ⌃G to show or hide layout grids.

children.name: Intro
children.text: A component is a reusable piece of design. Its instances follow every change to the main component, and can still change their text and colors.

children.name: Bullet
children.text: •  Insert instances from Assets (click or drag), or by duplicating one.

children.name: Bullet
children.text: •  Right-click several layers → Create multiple components makes one each.

children.name: Create a component from a frame or the selection
children.text: Create a component from a frame or the selection

children.name: Drag an instance out of a main component
children.text: Drag an instance out of a main component

children.name: Bullet
children.text: •  Combine components as variants into a set; names like “Style=Primary” become variant properties.

children.name: Bullet
children.text: •  Properties (the + in the Properties section): boolean (show or hide a layer), text, instance swap, icon (see page 10) and slots (an area instances can fill).

children.name: Bullet
children.text: •  Select a main component to see its properties; select an instance to set them.

children.name: Bullet
children.text: •  Change an instance’s text, colors or properties; ⋯ → Reset all changes puts them back, Push changes to main component sends them to the main.

children.name: Bullet
children.text: •  Click the instance’s name in the panel to swap it for another component.

children.name: Bullet
children.text: •  Assets → ⓘ opens a component in the playground to try its properties before inserting it.

children.name: Bullet
children.text: •  Publish components (Σ menu) to use them in other Sigma Design files as a library.

children.name: Bullet
children.text: •  A component’s ⋯ → Deprecate hides it from Assets while its instances keep working.

children.name: Select one of the instances on the right
children.text: Select one of the instances on the right and type a new Label in the panel. Then select the main Button set and change a variant’s color: every instance follows.

children.name: Button
children.description: Calls to action. Primary for the main action on a screen, Secondary for the others.

children.name: Card
children.description: A raised surface that groups related content, with an optional action.

children.name: Body

see every layer follow.

children.name: Note
children.text: Instances of the Button set and the Card, with their own labels.

children.name: Intro
children.text: A design token is a named value: a color, a size, a text style, a shadow. Layers that use tokens update when the token changes, and follow modes like Light and Dark.

children.name: Bullet
children.text: •  The token button (◈) next to a fill, stroke, number, visibility, text content or effect applies a token; it then shows as a purple chip.

children.name: Bullet
children.text: •  Text style in the Text section applies a typography token.

children.name: Bullet
children.text: •  Typing a value over a token detaches it.

children.name: Bullet
children.text: •  Collections with several modes (Light and Dark) get a picker in the Layer section; set it on a frame, a page or an instance, and its layers follow. Auto inherits from the parent.

children.name: Bullet
children.text: •  An extension like Brand B changes only some tokens (the accent). Pick it in the same place to re-skin a design.

children.name: Bullet
children.text: •  With nothing selected, the panel shows the Sigma Tokens file this file uses. Design tokens… (Σ menu) changes it; files with the same token names are interchangeable.

children.name: Bullet
children.text: •  Browse design tokens… (Σ menu, or the panel) shows them all: this file’s local tokens (most files have none) and the Sigma Tokens file’s, read-only. Local tokens can move to a Sigma Tokens file later.

children.name: Bullet
children.text: •  Audit design tokens… finds the values that don’t use a token yet. See page 7.

children.name: Select the Light frame and set Semantic
children.text: Select the Light frame and set Semantic to Dark in its Layer section. Then try Brand B on the Dark frame.

children.name: Intro
children.text: Fills, strokes, effects and text, each of which can come from a token.

children.name: Bullet
children.text: •  A layer can have several fills and strokes, stacked, each with its own opacity; + adds one.

children.name: Bullet
children.text: •  Strokes sit inside, centered or outside the edge, with one weight for all of them.

children.name: Bullet
children.text: •  Drop shadow, inner shadow and layer blur, as many as you like (Effects +).

children.name: Bullet
children.text: •  A shadow can use a shadow token, like the elevation tokens on the right.

children.name: Bullet
children.text: •  Text style applies a typography token: family, weight, size, line height and letter spacing at once.

children.name: Bullet
children.text: •  Auto width, auto height or fixed size; left, center or right.

children.name: Bullet
children.text: •  Case shows text as typed, UPPERCASE, lowercase or Title Case, without changing what you typed.

children.name: The Export section exports the selection
children.text: The Export section exports the selection (or the page) as PNG, JPG or SVG at 0.5× to 4×; ⇧⌘E exports a PNG.

children.name: Select a text style sample and look at i
children.text: Select a text style sample and look at its Text style chip. Select the Overlay card and change its shadow in Effects: the token detaches.

children.name: Note
children.text: Shadow tokens, darker in Dark mode.

children.name: Intro
children.text: Sigma helps keep a design accessible and on-system.

children.name: Bullet
children.text: •  Select one text layer: the Fill section shows its contrast with what’s behind it and its WCAG level. AA needs 4.5:1 (3:1 for large text), AAA 7:1.

children.name: Bullet
children.text: •  In a Sigma Tokens file, a color token’s inspector checks it against the colors it’s used with, in every mode.

children.name: Bullet
children.text: •  Audit design tokens… (Σ menu, or the panel with nothing selected) lists every color, text style, spacing, radius and shadow that doesn’t use a token, with the token that matches.

children.name: Bullet
children.text: •  Use, Choose… or Use all exact matches binds them; Select shows the layers.

children.name: Bullet
children.text: •  It also finds layers using deprecated tokens and instances of deprecated components.

children.name: Deprecate tokens (in their inspector) an
children.text: Deprecate tokens (in their inspector) and components (⋯ menu) you’re retiring: they’re hidden from pickers and Assets, while everything that uses them keeps working with a note.

children.name: Select each text on the right and look a
children.text: Select each text on the right and look at Contrast in its Fill section. Then run Audit design tokens…: it finds the two one-off values on purpose.

children.name: Note
children.text: The last one fails AA: white on this blue is under 3:1.

children.name: Note
children.text: These use raw values on purpose. Run the audit.

children.name: Intro
children.text: Design systems change. Sigma publishes changes as numbered versions, lets the files that use them decide when to update, and keeps a history of every file.

children.name: Bullet
children.text: •  Publish… in a Sigma Tokens file creates a version (v1, v2…) with notes and a list of what changed.

children.name: Bullet
children.text: •  Sigma Design files that use it get a banner when a new version is out; they review it and accept it.

children.name: Bullet
children.text: •  Sigma Tokens files can link other Sigma Tokens files (a Brand file pointing at a Core file).

children.name: Bullet
children.text: •  Publish components… (Σ menu) publishes this file’s components.

children.name: Bullet
children.text: •  Component libraries… in another Sigma Design file links it; its components then appear in Assets.

children.name: Bullet
children.text: •  Every file autosaves versions as you work. Show version history (Σ menu) to view one, restore it, or duplicate it as a new file.

children.name: Bullet
children.text: •  Download a copy (.sigma.json) and Import file… move files between browsers.

children.name: Bullet
children.text: •  A Sigma Tokens file exports tokens.json (W3C Design Tokens) and CSS variables, and imports tokens.json.

children.name: Bullet
children.text: •  Move to Archive (on the files home) is a soft delete; restore from the Archive.

children.name: Every file of your own gets a version hi
children.text: Every file of your own gets a version history (Σ menu → Show version history). This sample has none, because it’s never saved: duplicate it to try version history on your copy.

children.name: Change tokens in the Sigma Tokens file.
children.text: Change tokens in the Sigma Tokens file.

children.name: Accepting updates every layer that uses
children.text: Accepting updates every layer that uses those tokens.

children.name: Intro
children.text: A Sigma Tokens file is a design system’s values, with no canvas. Open Sigma Tokens in the Welcome to Sigma folder (on the files home) to explore the one this file uses.

children.name: Bullet
children.text: •  Collections hold groups and tokens (Collection → Group → Tokens), with descriptions.

children.name: Bullet
children.text: •  Three levels work well: Primitives (raw values: color/blue/500), Semantic (what they mean: accent/default) and Components (where they’re used: button/primary/background).

children.name: Color (with opacity), number, text, bool
children.text: Color (with opacity), number, text, boolean, typography, shadow, duration and easing. Typography and shadow tokens are made of parts that can point at other tokens.

children.name: Bullet
children.text: •  Type { in a value to point it at another token; the inspector shows the whole chain and what refers to a token.

children.name: Bullet
children.text: •  Change a primitive and everything pointing at it follows.

children.name: Bullet
children.text: •  Modes are columns (Light, Dark). Extend creates a collection that inherits everything and overrides only some values (Brand B); ↺ resets an override.

children.name: Bullet
children.text: •  Contrast pairs check colors used together in every mode; Deprecated retires a token safely.

children.name: Bullet
children.text: •  Export tokens.json (W3C format) and CSS variables for code; import tokens.json from other tools.

children.name: Select a swatch on the right: its fill i
children.text: Select a swatch on the right: its fill is a primitive token. Back to files → Welcome to Sigma → Sigma Tokens shows them all.

children.name: Note
children.text: A 4-point scale. Each bar’s width is the token.

children.name: Intro
children.text: Icons are a library of their own: a Sigma Icons file holds them, and components pick from it. Open Sigma Icons in the Welcome to Sigma folder to explore the one this file uses.

children.name: Bullet
children.text: •  Import SVGs from any free set (Lucide, Tabler, Heroicons, Phosphor, Material Symbols), drop them in, or paste SVG code. Colors are removed: an icon takes the color of the layer that shows it.

children.name: Bullet
children.text: •  Icons are outline or filled, in groups, with keywords for search. Publish… makes them available to Sigma Design files.

children.name: Bullet
children.text: •  Sigma Icons, in the Welcome to Sigma folder, is the whole Lucide set: about 1,900 icons. + Sigma Icons ▾ → Lucide (on the files home) adds it as a file of your own.

children.name: Bullet
children.text: •  Icon libraries… (Σ menu) links a Sigma Icons file. A file keeps copies of only the icons it uses.

children.name: Bullet
children.text: •  Select a main component, or a layer in one, then + in the Icon section (or right-click → Insert icon…).

children.name: Bullet
children.text: •  An icon’s color is its fill, which can use a color token; outline icons also have a stroke width. Swap icon… changes it.

children.name: Bullet
children.text: •  Apply icon property (next to Swap icon…) lets instances choose the icon, from all icons or only some groups.

children.name: Bullet
children.text: •  Instances choose only the icon: its size, color and stroke stay the main component’s.

children.name: Select one of the icon buttons on the ri
children.text: Select one of the icon buttons on the right and choose another icon in its Icon property: only the Actions icons are offered. Then select the main Icon button’s icon and change its color token: every instance follows.

children.name: Main components with icons. Select one t
children.text: Main components with icons. Select one to see its Icon property.

children.name: Icon button
children.description: A square button with only an icon. Its Icon property offers the Actions icons.

children.name: Menu item
children.description: A row in a menu: an icon (any icon) and a label.

children.name: Rating
children.description: Filled and outline stars together: the two styles of the same icon.

children.name: Icon styles
children.description: The same icons in the outline and the filled style.

children.name: Note
children.text: Instances of Icon button, each with its own icon.

children.name: Note
children.text: The Menu item’s icon and label are properties.
